title: Reverse an Array
description:
Given an array `nums`, return a new array with the same numbers in the opposite order.

Example: for `nums = [1, 2, 3]` return `[3, 2, 1]`.

If the array is empty, return an empty array.
hints: Concept: you can create a new array of the same size with `new int[nums.length]`. The last position of an array is `nums.length - 1`.
Approach: the first number of the answer is the last number of `nums`, the second is the second-to-last, and so on. Fill the new array from the front while reading `nums` from the back.

Pseudocode:
  result = new array of size n
  for i from 0 to n - 1:
      result[i] = nums[n - 1 - i]
  return result

workedExample.title: Double Every Number
workedExample.description: Given `nums`, return a new array where each number is doubled.
workedExample.explanation:
The method builds a brand new array the same size as the input, then fills it one position at a time.

Here position `i` of the result comes from position `i` of the input. In your problem, position `i` of the result comes from a different position of the input. Work out which one.

walkthrough.note: Create an empty result array with 4 slots.
i = 3: copy nums[0] = 1 into result[3]. Done!

mistakes.hint: The order didn't change. If you swap in place, only go halfway; going all the way swaps every pair twice. Or fill a new array from the back.
One of your positions is off by one. The last valid index is `nums.length - 1`, so the mirror of position `i` is `nums.length - 1 - i`.
